title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X proper over an algebraically closed field k, and N prime to char k. The page computes H^1 and, by duality, H^{2n-1}, in terms of the Picard and Albanese varieties and NS(X).

(1) Kummer sequence 0→μ_N→G_m→G_m→0. H^0(X,G_m) is the unit group of a finite k-algebra, so it is N-divisible for N prime to p. Hence H^1(X,μ_N) ≅ _N Pic(X).

(2) From 0→Pic^0(X)→Pic(X)→NS(X)→0, with Pic^0(X) the k-points of a connected group scheme and therefore divisible, the snake lemma gives 0→_N Pic^0(X)→H^1(X,μ_N)→_N NS(X)→0.

(3) Pass to the limit over N=ℓ^ν. NS(X) is finitely generated and Pic^τ/Pic^0 is finite, so T_ℓ(NS)=0. Hence H^1(X,Z_ℓ(1)) ≅ T_ℓ(Pic^0_{X/k}); only the reduced part counts.

(4) Suppose Pic^0_{X/k} is proper, e.g. X normal. Put B_X = (Pic^0_{X/k})_red = Pic^{00}, an abelian variety, and A_X = B_X^* (dual), the Albanese variety. Let φ_X: X→A_X be the Albanese map. Then φ_X^*: H^1(A_X,Z_ℓ) → H^1(X,Z_ℓ) is an isomorphism. This uses H^1(A,Z_ℓ) = Hom(T_ℓA,Z_ℓ) ≅ T_ℓ(A^*)(-1) via the Weil pairing.

(5) Now let X be smooth projective of dimension n. Poincaré duality gives H^{2n-1}(X,Z/N) ≅ H^1(X,Z/N)^∨(-n). Dualizing (2), and using the Weil pairing (_N B_X)^∨ ≅ _N A_X(-1), one gets
0→(_N NS(X))^∨(1-n)→H^{2n-1}(X,Z/N)→_N A_X(k)(-n)→0.
The last term is identified with H^1(B_X,Z/N) up to a twist.

(6) Pass to the limit over ℓ^ν; Mittag-Leffler holds since all groups are finite. This gives
0→(NS(X)[ℓ^∞])^∨→H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n-1)→H^1(B_X,Z_ℓ)→0.
The left term is finite (the dual of the ℓ-primary torsion of NS). The right term is free. So the torsion of H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ) is dual to NS_tors{ℓ}, and the free quotient is H^1 of the Picard variety.

Purpose: to relate H^1 and H^{2n-1} to Alb and Pic. This is part of the preparation for the Lefschetz/standard-conjecture material in this dossier. The next page records the dictionary 'Alb ↔ H^1, Pic ↔ H^{2n-1}(n-1)'.
errors: The vertical identification _N A_X(k)(-n) ≅ H^1(B_X,Z/NZ) is only correct up to a Tate twist: _N A_X(-1) ≅ (_N B_X)^∨ = H^1(B_X,Z/N), so H^1(B_X,Z/N)(1-n) ≅ _N A_X(-n). Grothendieck struck the twist here, and compensates in the limit sequence by twisting the middle term by (n-1). The final ℓ-adic sequence is consistent.

Minor: the first isomorphism H^1(X,μ_N)≅_N Pic(X) tacitly uses that H^0(X,G_m) is N-divisible. This holds for X proper over an algebraically closed field with N prime to p, so it is correct as stated.

ideas.what: Kummer theory: H^1(X,μ_N) ≅ _N Pic(X), and the extension of _N NS by _N Pic^0
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 / SGA 4½ (Cohomologie étale, arcata), Le groupe de Brauer II-III

ideas.what: H^1(X,Z_ℓ(1)) ≅ T_ℓ Pic^0_{X/k}, and H^1(X,Z_ℓ) ≅ H^1(Alb,Z_ℓ) via the Albanese map
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic H^1 = Tate module of Picard variety; Albanese map iso on H^1
ideas.where_published: SGA 4½; also standard (Milne, Étale cohomology; Kleiman, Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Dual description: torsion of H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ) is dual to the ℓ-torsion of NS, and its free quotient is H^1 of the Picard variety twisted by (n-1)
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré duality combined with Kummer; H^{2n-1} ↔ Picard/Albanese, torsion of H^{2n-1} dual to NS_tors
ideas.where_published: Essentially in Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés 1968) and standard texts

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, standard working computations of H^1 and H^{2n-1} via the Kummer sequence and Poincaré duality, with a minor twist bookkeeping slip. Everything here is well-known and in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'H^{dim-1}' should read H^{2n-1} throughout. The text is about the degree dual to H^1 on an n-dimensional smooth projective X.
The bracketed hypothesis on the first lines is 'X propre sur corps k alg. clos, N premier à car. de k'.

In the limit sequence the left term is (NS(X)[ℓ])^∨, with the gloss 'comp. ℓ-primaire'. It is a finite group, not 'libre'. The word under H^1(B_X,Z_ℓ) is unclear, probably 'libre ... topologiques/algébriques'.
In the previous page's transcription, 'Br' should be 'Pic' and NS: the formula is H^1(X,μ_n)≅_n Pic(X), not H^2/Br. That page appears to duplicate this one.
